slides.title: Beyond URL Security 🔒
slides.content:
# Secure at the Method Level

Instead of (or in addition to) URL rules, you can annotate methods with `@PreAuthorize` to restrict access based on roles, permissions, or even custom logic.

This is especially useful when you want different access rules for different methods inside the same controller.

quizData.question: Which annotation must you add to enable method security?
quizData.explanation: You need to add @EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true) to a configuration class to enable @PreAuthorize.

slides.title: Powerful Expressions 💪
slides.content:
# Common Expressions in @PreAuthorize

| Expression | Meaning |
|------------|---------|
| `hasRole('ROLE')` | Checks if the user has the given role (without ROLE_ prefix if you use `hasRole`) |
| `hasAnyRole('ROLE1','ROLE2')` | Any of the roles |
| `hasAuthority('PERMISSION')` | Checks for a specific authority |
| `#id == authentication.principal.id` | Access based on parameter value and authenticated user |
| `@beanName.method(...)` | Call a custom bean for complex logic |

You can combine them with `and`, `or`, `!`.

slides.title: Service Layer Security 🛡️
slides.content: Method security works on Spring beans (services, controllers). Place annotations on service methods to ensure business logic is protected even if someone bypasses the controller.
